title: Seven Clear at the Eighth, Eight Behind at the End
title_candidates: Seven Clear at the Eighth, Eight Behind at the End
Two at the Eighth, Twenty-Seven After It
The Eagle and the Aftermath: Baker's Bletchingley
Mullin Keeps Still While Everyone Else Falls Over
theme: Mullin and Baker walked to the last day dead level; the Trophy was settled not by anything Mullin did brilliantly but by the eight holes on Bletchingley's back nine where Baker mislaid 27 shots — and Mullin, the steadiest man in the field for four days, was the only one standing there to collect it.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Ronay/Peck; celebratory of Mullin, mercilessly fond about the wreckage
opening_hook: Open on the 8th green at Bletchingley in R4: Baker holes out for an eagle 2 on a par 4 and stands seven clear of the man who will beat him by eight — then rewind to Ashdown and explain how a tournament that was level after 54 holes came apart in eight.
foreshadow: Baker arrives as defending Trophy champion (TEG 3) and the only other man in the field with a Trophy to his name — the reigning holder framing for a coronation that isn't.
Mullin arrives on back-to-back Green Jackets; the gross contest is effectively settled in the first three hours at Ashdown and never troubles anyone again.
Williams's R1 at Ashdown — 22 shots bled over holes 10-18 — planted as a habit, not an accident: he closes badly, and one day it will cost him something.

Bletchingley is billed as 'excellent drainage and fast playing conditions'; the only fast thing about it turns out to be the rate at which the field's cards disintegrate, the par-5 15th in particular.

competitions.name: Trophy (Net VP)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (winner, +9, by 8 over Jon Baker)
competitions.how: Baker led by 3 after Ashdown; Mullin took the lead at Lingfield when Baker posted his worst round to date (+9); Baker's -3 at Crowborough pulled the pair exactly level at 8 apiece with 18 to play. In R4 Baker birdied the 2nd for the outright lead and eagled the 8th to stand seven clear — then dropped 27 shots from the 9th to the 16th, including a 9 at the par-3 12th and an 11 at the 15th. Mullin retook the lead outright at the 12th and never gave it back, closing +1, the best round in the field. +9 is the lowest winning Trophy total in TEG history to date.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (winner, +81, by 19 over Stuart Neumann)
competitions.how: No contest and no suspense: Mullin led from the 11th at Ashdown and was never headed. He beat Neumann head-to-head in all four rounds and was best in the field in three of them, the centrepiece being 88 (+17) at Crowborough — the second-best gross round in TEG history to date. Four of the five players nonetheless posted personal-best gross totals; only Mullin's mattered.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams (loser, +40 net VP, by 5 from Henry Meller)
competitions.how: Williams was below the field median in all four rounds but only third-last after two. He slid to fourth at Crowborough (18 shots gone in six holes) and then handed it to himself at Bletchingley: bottom outright at the 6th, briefly reprieved when Meller's 10 at the 11th sent the reigning double-Spoon holder to the floor, then back to the bottom for good at the 13th, the start of a closing six in which he shed 16 more. His +15 is his worst round to date; his +43 gross his worst gross round to date. The comedy of it: Williams did all this while recording a personal-best gross total of +152, and Meller escaped after back-to-back Spoons despite owning the worst single hole in TEG history.

headline_candidates: No Bunkers at Ashdown, and Meller Still Finds a 12
A Course With No Sand and a Card With No Hope
Baker Leads; Meller Counts to Twelve
rounds.chosen_headline: No Bunkers at Ashdown, and Meller Still Finds a 12
rounds.angle: TEG's first day in East Sussex on a bunkerless heathland: Baker heads the Trophy by 3, Mullin posts the best gross of the day and takes a Jacket lead he holds for 62 holes, and Meller runs up a 12 at the par-3 11th — the worst hole in TEG history — while Williams quietly bleeds 22 shots coming home.

headline_candidates: Baker's Worst Round Yet Hands Mullin the Lead
Lingfield's Water, Baker's Nine at the 17th
rounds.chosen_headline: Baker's Worst Round Yet Hands Mullin the Lead at Lingfield
rounds.angle: Baker's +9 — a personal worst at the time, capped by a 9 at the 17th — flips the Trophy to Mullin, who needs only a tidy +4; Williams and Meller contribute a quintuple apiece and Neumann props up the round.

headline_candidates: Mullin's 88 on the Beacon — and Baker Draws Level Anyway
Level Pegging Above the South Downs
rounds.chosen_headline: Mullin's 88 on the Beacon — and Baker Draws Level Anyway
rounds.angle: Crowborough gives the tournament its best golf: Mullin's +17 gross is the second-best gross round in TEG history and he goes nine holes without dropping a net shot, but Baker's -3 (his own nine clean holes to open, quads at the 15th and 18th notwithstanding) squares the Trophy at 8 apiece with one round left — while Williams loses 18 shots in the first six and slides towards the Spoon.

headline_candidates: Baker Eagles the 8th, Then Loses 27 Shots in Eight Holes
Seven Up at the Eighth, Eight Down at the End
Fast Greens, Slow Death: Bletchingley Eats the Field
rounds.chosen_headline: Baker Eagles the 8th, Then Loses 27 Shots in Eight Holes
rounds.angle: The whole tournament in one back nine: Baker birdies the 2nd for the outright lead, eagles the par-4 8th to go seven clear, then posts 9-7-8-9-6-6-11-6 from the 9th; Mullin, six clean net holes to start and a stray 7 at the 7th aside, grinds out +1 — best in the field — takes the lead outright at the 12th and completes the double. Behind them Bletchingley finishes the Spoon: Williams bottom at the 6th, Meller's 10 at the 11th, Williams's 16-shot close from the 13th, and four personal-best gross totals filed under 'small mercies'.

players.arc: Never finished a round worse than second of five, turned back-to-back Jackets into three by 19 shots, and was the only man upright on Bletchingley's back nine — a second Trophy, at the lowest winning total TEG has yet seen.
The defending champion led by seven with ten to play and lost by eight: an eagle at the 8th, then 27 shots in eight holes, with a personal-best gross total of +113 as the receipt.
Below the field median in all four rounds and a specialist in closing nines, he collected his first Wooden Spoon at Bletchingley — on the same day he completed a personal-best gross total of +152.

Owner of the worst hole in TEG history (a 12 at Ashdown's par-3 11th), briefly last again after a 10 at Bletchingley's 11th, and yet — with a personal-best +107 gross — the man who finally escapes the Spoon after two in a row.
Jacket runner-up with a personal-best +100 gross, beaten head-to-head by Mullin in all four rounds and, for one bleak afternoon at Lingfield, the man at the bottom of everything.

venue_notes: TEG's first visit to East Sussex (and neighbouring Surrey), and — unusually — four brand-new courses in four days, so no course history exists for anybody: every number set here is a first. Thread the character of each: Royal Ashdown Forest's celebrated absence of bunkers (which did not prevent a 12 at its par-3 11th), Lingfield's water and grand parkland trees, Crowborough Beacon's MacKenzie holes and South Downs panoramas as the stage for the best golf of the TEG, and Bletchingley's advertised 'fast playing conditions' as the ironic frame for the R4 collapse. Keep location colour light and always attached to a scoring fact.
course_history_notes: Four debut courses: no player had prior history at Ashdown, Lingfield, Crowborough or Bletchingley, so there are no course PBs to beat — only new benchmarks set.
With no course history to lean on, the records that mattered were tournament-wide: four of the five players posted personal-best gross totals (Neumann +100, Meller +107, Baker +113, Williams +152).
Mullin's best card of the TEG came at Crowborough — 88 gross, +17 — the second-best gross round in TEG history to date.
Ashdown's par-3 11th (SI 3) now carries the worst hole in TEG history: Meller's 12.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R4 H12 at Bletchingley — Baker's 9 at a par 3 (SI 18, the easiest hole on the course) hands Mullin the outright lead for good, eight holes after Baker had stood seven clear.
Green Jacket: R1 H11 at Ashdown — Mullin moves to the front on gross and is never headed again across the remaining 62 holes, winning by 19.
Wooden Spoon: R4 H13 at Bletchingley — Williams's triple bogey puts him back on the bottom for the last time, the start of a closing six in which he sheds 16 shots and loses the Spoon by 5.

payoffs.payoff: The reigning holder leads outright at the 2nd and by seven at the 8th, then surrenders the title with 27 shots dropped from the 9th to the 16th — dethroned by the man he beat last year.

payoffs.resolves_in: Round 1 (set up) and 'How the three were decided' (Green Jacket section)
payoffs.payoff: Jacket number three, led from Ashdown's 11th, best in field in three of four rounds, 19 shots clear of Neumann — the least suspenseful competition of the four days.

payoffs.seed: Williams's 22 shots dropped over holes 10-18 at Ashdown
payoffs.payoff: The same closing-nine habit returns at Bletchingley: bottom outright at the 6th, 16 shots gone from the 13th, a worst-ever +15 round and the Wooden Spoon by 5.

payoffs.seed: Bletchingley's 'fast playing conditions' and the par-5 15th
payoffs.payoff: The 15th takes an 11 from Baker, a 10 from Meller and an 8 from Williams in the same round; the only fast thing at Bletchingley was the collapse.

vehicle_fit_response.note: The Mullin-Baker duel is real (20 lead changes, level after 54 holes) but TEG 2 already ran dual_narrative, and the honest frame here is counterfactual — seven clear at the 8th, beaten by eight — with inversion (defending champion dethroned) riding alongside.

why_the_champion_won: Level with Baker after 54 holes, Mullin won it by being the only man Bletchingley's back nine didn't dismantle: +1, best in the field, while Baker gave back 27 shots in eight holes — inherited, yes, but Mullin was the steadiest player in the field, never finishing a round worse than second of five, and he was the one standing there to take it.
